title: Assembly of an inexpensive rat jugular catheter button based on a split-septum needleless intravenous system
author: Suarez, Cantrell, et al.

steps.title: Obtain 22 G cannula
steps.instruction: Separate a 22 G steel cannula from a blunt‑tip 22 G needle or from commercial 22 G hypodermic tubing by using needle‑nose pliers to pull the metal tube out with rotation, or warm the plastic hub with a lighter flame to soften the adhesive; avoid crimping the cannula.

steps.title: Trim cannula to 2 cm length
steps.instruction: Cut the isolated cannula to a 2 cm length using a rotary tool (e.g., Dremel®) equipped with a Cut‑Off Wheel disk; wear safety goggles and do not use wire snips or scissors to avoid creating crimps.

steps.title: Clean and inspect trimmed cannula
steps.instruction: Remove metal debris by sonicating the cannula or rocking it for 15 min in distilled water, then rinse three times with fresh distilled water, examine under a light microscope for burrs, and smooth any jagged ends with a 100‑grit nail file or fine sandpaper; verify the cannula is straight, intact, and free of holes.

steps.title: Bend cannula into L‑shape
steps.instruction: Grip both ends of the 2 cm cannula with two needle‑nose pliers and slowly bend it into an L‑shape: ~0.5 cm straight, ~0.5 cm curved bend, and ~1 cm long segment; ensure the curve is gentle and not a sharp angle.

steps.title: Cut and bevel venous catheter tubing
steps.instruction: Using a fresh, sharp razor blade, cut MRE 040S tubing to 11.5 cm for male rats or 9.5 cm for female rats; bevel one end at 45°, then mark 2.5 cm distal to the bevel with a permanent lab marker to indicate the catheter‑anchor bead position.

steps.title: Prepare mesh and bead tubing
steps.instruction: Cut two Dacron® surgical‑mesh circles of 23–25 mm diameter and punch a 10 mm central hole in each; cut a 1–2 mm segment of Micro‑Renathane 0.065″ × 0.030″ bead tubing for the catheter bead and a 3–4 mm segment of stopper‑bead tubing for the cannula stopper.

steps.title: Attach catheter bead to catheter
steps.instruction: Slide the catheter bead over the beveled end of the catheter tube, positioning it near the 2.5 cm mark; apply a very small drop of cyanoacrylate glue at the mark, slide the bead into place with forceps or fingers, and allow the glue to dry.

steps.title: Assemble cannula with stopper bead in Interlink port
steps.instruction: Place the stopper bead on the shorter end of the L‑bent cannula close to the bend; insert this end into the open (bottom) side of the 2.5 cm male Interlink split‑septum port; secure the cannula in a soldering‑stand arm, lower it into the port, and apply a small drop of cyanoacrylate around the port to anchor and seal; confirm the cannula is straight and perpendicular to the port opening.

steps.title: Secure first mesh disk and apply cyanoacrylate
steps.instruction: Rest the first Dacron mesh disk around the rim of the bottom of the Interlink assembly; apply a few drops of cyanoacrylate glue along the inner rim of the port, then let it dry.

steps.title: Build dental cement cone and add second mesh disk
steps.instruction: Prepare a relatively fluid dental cement (monomer + polymer) and, using a plastic transfer pipette, apply it over the first mesh disk so it flows through the mesh and contacts the base of the Interlink assembly, forming a ~1.5 cm diameter layer; increase cement viscosity with additional powder and shape a conical build around the cannula bend, tapering to a ~0.5 cm diameter tip; once set, thread the cannula through the central hole of the second mesh disk, place the disk atop the cone, and secure it with additional dental cement; allow the dental acrylic to cure completely.

steps.title: Insert catheter onto cannula within button
steps.instruction: Using forceps, slide the non‑beveled end of the catheter onto the metal cannula inside the button assembly, pushing it in a few millimetres; friction should hold it, but a tiny drop of cyanoacrylate may be added at the junction for extra security.

steps.title: Leak test assembled catheter button
steps.instruction: Before sterilization, submerge the bottom part of the assembled button in water; attach a blunt‑tip plastic cannula to an empty, air‑filled 1 ml syringe, pierce the Interlink septum, depress the plunger to push air through, and watch for bubbles at any dental‑cement/plastic interfaces or at the catheter‑cannula junction.

steps.title: Cold‑sterilize catheter button with glutaraldehyde
steps.instruction: Immerse the assembled button in a 2.65 % glutaraldehyde solution (e.g., Wavicide®) following the manufacturer’s guidelines for polyurethane‑based tubing.

steps.title: Ethanol fill and soak catheter button
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps and gloves, remove the button from glutaraldehyde, fill its entire length with 70 % ethanol via a 1 ml syringe, then soak the ethanol‑filled button in a 70 % ethanol bath for at least 8 h; store in a cool, dry environment if not implanted within a week.

steps.title: Flush catheter with sterile saline before implantation
steps.instruction: Immediately prior to surgical implantation, flush the catheter lumen with sterile saline to hydrate the tubing and remove residual ethanol.
